title: Revived my very first abandoned gameproject from 10 years ago. Very happy with the result after a week.
author: trxr2005
selftext: Since I became a dad not long ago, I had only very little time for making games in my free time, because there was no free time at all..but thanks to AI, I'm positive about being able to publish a game again.

comments.author: SirSilksalot
comments.body:
I like the mechanics. Feels like adding some blocks are physics based objects that interact with the drawn features would make it more engaging and replayable IMO. Otherwise, doesn’t seem to matter what shape you draw.

Take it or leave it.

replies.author: trxr2005
replies.body: It does matter what is being drawed. For now there are pointy and blunt stones, which either get stuck in the enemy and slow them down or stun them. There are also certain types of enemies who can only be damages by certain stone types.

comments.author: CountryOk4844
comments.body:
Why wouldn't someone just keep drawing rectangles as big as the drawing area? Why draw anything smaller, or a different shape?

I know, it would take the fun out of it, but still, such an obvious winning strategy should not exist in my opinion.

This shape-drawing mechanic would be better in a game where you have to make something fit through different holes, or something like that, so there's no constant best solution. For this tower defense game I believe that just getting a few boulders in different shapes and sizes periodically and having to decide where and how to drop them (a bit like Tetris, but the opposite of filling the gaps) would be more fun, you would have to make more interesting decisions. The drawing mechanic is interesting, but since the goal is so simple and never changes ("draw the biggest boulder you can") at the end of the day it doesn't make it more fun.

Of course, this is just my opinion, and it's possible that I missed something, or there's more that's not in the video. Either way, good luck!

replies.author: trxr2005
replies.body: Hi, thank you for your input 😊 Well, to prevent exactly this there is a limited mana pool. Drawing drains your mana the bigger stones you draw. You get some mana back for killing enemies and even more for making a combo, but drawing big boulders constantly would use up your mana too quickly. There are also enemies who carry shields, which make them immune to the first hit, so using smaller stones to destroy that shield are necessary for keeping your mana up.
